claims.text: A high-entropy M3O4 spinel containing seven first-row transition metals can be used as a replacement support or interfacial layer in an automotive exhaust catalyst.
Replacing a conventional catalyst support with the high-entropy spinel will enhance catalytic activity.
Replacing a conventional catalyst support with the high-entropy spinel will improve catalyst durability.
Replacing a conventional catalyst support with the high-entropy spinel will reduce the required platinum-group-metal loading.
Conventional platinum-based automotive catalysts use ordered spinel or ceria-based supports in monolith structures.
The high-entropy spinel has high configurational disorder and mixed cation occupancy.
Configurational disorder and mixed cation occupancy promote a high density of oxygen vacancies in the spinel.
Increased oxygen-vacancy formation and mobility facilitate rapid oxidation of exhaust pollutants.
The high-entropy support provides stable anchoring sites for platinum-group-metal species.
Stable anchoring sites suppress platinum-group-metal sintering during thermal cycling.
Enhanced oxygen-vacancy behavior will lower catalyst light-off temperature.
The high-entropy-supported catalyst will exhibit faster pollutant conversion than a conventional platinum catalyst with an ordered support under identical conditions.
The predicted benefits apply under exhaust temperatures of 400–800 °C and fluctuating feeds containing CO, hydrocarbons, and NOx.
The predicted improvements depend on the support retaining configurational disorder and phase purity during extended thermal cycling.
Phase transformations or synthesis variability could limit the predicted improvements.
Long-term structural stability and reproducibility under prolonged, fluctuating automotive exhaust conditions are uncertain.
